SmallestThree quaternion encoding offers better precision for small components compared to FirstThree, at the cost of slightly more complex decoding logic [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states in the notes section: 'SmallestThree uses 4 bytes for 10-bit precision on 3 components plus 2 bits for index, allowing better precision for small components. FirstThree uses 3 bytes with 8-bit fixed point.' It also describes the decoding logic for SmallestThree as involving a loop and index extraction, which is more complex than the FirstThree method described as 'Convert 3 uint8s to float...'. Thus, the claim that SmallestThree offers better precision for small components at the cost of more complex decoding logic is fully supported by the text.
